lines.text: A tiny hole. A dark room.
The world outside appears on the wall, upside down.
People knew this two thousand years ago.
But nobody could keep the picture.
Eighteen thirty-nine. Paris announces the daguerreotype.
An image fixed on silver. Sit still for minutes.
Eighteen eighty-eight. A box camera with a hundred shots inside.
One click. Then mail the camera back for prints.
Then thirty-five millimetre film. A camera for your coat pocket.
Nineteen seventy-five. An engineer, Steven Sasson, builds a digital camera.
Eight pounds. Ten thousand pixels. Twenty-three seconds to save each one.
By two thousand, phones take photos.
Today, we take over a trillion a year.
Look closer. It's still a tiny hole and a dark room.
Just small enough for your pocket.
